stem:
A steel ball on the end of a thin string oscillates with small oscillations, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The displacement of the centre of the ball from its equilibrium position is *x*.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 5.2 shows the variation with *x* of the acceleration *a* of the ball.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text: Explain how Fig. 5.2 shows that the oscillations of the ball are simple harmonic.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the period *T* of the oscillations.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: At time *t* = 0, when the displacement of the ball has its maximum value, the ball is immersed in a trough containing thick oil so that the ball is just below the surface of the oil. This results in the subsequent motion of the ball being heavily damped.
parts.text: State what is meant by damping.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.3, sketch a possible variation of the displacement *x* of the ball with *t* between *t* = 0 and *t* = 2*T*.

[[fig:f3]]

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1 (not to scale)
figures.alt: A steel ball suspended from a thin string is shown displaced from its dashed equilibrium position, with the oscillations indicated.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of acceleration a against displacement x with a straight line sloping downwards through the origin.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: A blank graph with displacement x on the vertical axis and time t on the horizontal axis, marked from 0 to 2T.
